subject: MAP: performance benchmarking plan + fleet sizing recommendation for Acme Data

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>

Subject: MAP kickoff — perf benchmarks to lock timeline & HW recs for Acme

Team —

Quick MAP kickoff note for the Acme opportunity (attached brief MAP v0). Sales has a close target of 2026-09-24 and procurement needs a performance appendix to sign off. The buyer is explicit: they need TTFT / p95 latency at 512 tokens, steady-state throughput (tokens/sec), and concurrency targets for 100 and 300 active users. They also want cost per 1M tokens at production QPS.

Ask: Ben/Karthik — can you run the focused perf matrix below on A100 (40GB), H100 (80GB), and L40S (full), and include MIG-equivalence where feasible? Keep these exact rows:
- TTFT cold vs warm (seq=512)
- p50/p95 token latency (seq=512)
- Max sustainable throughput @ target latency SLOs (for p95 <= 400ms)
- Observed concurrency limits and degradation mode (MIG slices tested)
- Cost estimate per 1M tokens based on our cloud pricing + reserved vs burst profile

Constraints: use 8k context where possible (they may move to longer context), but the primary benchmark point is 512. Run both batched and unbatched (batch sizes 1,4,8) to show trade-offs. Include single-instance and distributed sharded runs if MGPU is required.

Marissa — please prepare a two-slide summary recommendation (1: perf tradeoffs, 2: recommended fleet & MAP timeline). I want a short decision: go H100 full for critical low-latency lanes, A100 MIG for bulk cheaper throughput, and L40S as a possible hybrid for cost-sensitive dev environment — but confirm with data.

Timeline: need perf results and slides by 2026-09-03 EOD PT to finalize MAP and sync with Acme 2026-09-07 for a canary plan.

Attachments: acme_map_v1.pdf (MAP skeleton).

Thanks —
Soojin

Subject: Re: MAP kickoff — perf benchmarks to lock timeline & HW recs for Acme

Got it. Quick run summary attached (perf_summary_20260901.csv). High-level findings from today's lab runs:

- H100 (single full 80GB): TTFT cold ~ 220ms, warm p95 ~ 120ms at seq=512, batch=1. Sustained throughput ~ 1.8k tokens/sec before p95 > 400ms. Cost estimate: higher hourly but lowest latency.
- A100 (full 40GB): TTFT cold ~ 300ms, warm p95 ~ 180ms at seq=512, batch=1. Sustained throughput ~ 1.5k tokens/sec. Good balance for mixed workloads.
- L40S (full): TTFT cold ~ 360ms, warm p95 ~ 210ms; throughput ~ 1.4k tokens/sec. More variable for long context.
- A100 MIG (7g.40gb-equivalent slices used): TTFT warm p95 ~ 240ms, throughput per slice ~ 450 tokens/sec. 3 slices -> ~1.3k tokens/sec with increased variability.

Notes: batching to 4 increased tokens/sec by ~25% but raised p95 by 20–40ms depending on model internals. Measured TTFT includes model load + kv cache population. All runs used our production build (v2.8) with attention optimizations.

I'll add the raw CSV and an annotated latency_vs_cost_matrix.xlsx for the slide deck. If you want additional MIG shapes, I can run 2-slice vs 3-slice tomorrow.

(attachment: perf_summary_20260901.csv)

-Ben

Thanks Ben — quick tech read:

- H100 full gives the best p95 headroom; for their SLO (p95 <= 400ms at seq=512) H100 can support ~2k tokens/sec with comfortable margin. It also supports sparse attention kernels better for longer contexts.
- A100 is cost-effective when using MIG slices for steady-state throughput; however, cold-start TTFT is worse because of model load times and KV cache rebuild. If Acme needs aggressive cold start SLAs, recommend a warm pool (reserved instances) or hybrid routing to H100 for traffic spikes.
- L40S is attractive for dev and non-critical lanes; we observed memory pressure at 8k context which balloons latency.
- MIG observations: 1) MIG is great for density but increases variance, 2) fragmentation makes autoscaling trickier, 3) consider 2 dedicated full A100s + MIG slices for burst.

Sizing recommendation (rough): for their initial forecast (100 active users -> ~600 concurrent requests, avg prompt length 200 tokens, response ~150 tokens):
- Latency-critical lane (10% of traffic): 3x H100 full GPUs (reserve)
- Bulk throughput lane: 6x A100 MIG-equivalent slices (distributed across 3 full A100s)
- Dev/staging: 2x L40S nodes

I'll add these to the MAP appendix slide. Also linking a quick cost sketch: H100 reserved hourly -> effective cost per 1M tokens = $X (see attached latency_vs_cost_matrix.xlsx).

-Karthik

1) Our production workload will be bursty (peaks at start of business day). Cold starts matter for the canary we plan to run. What is your recommendation for warm pools vs fast-failover to H100?
2) We are constrained by our procurement cap on ops spend; we need an option that keeps cost per 1M tokens around or below $Y. Please include that pricing line.
3) Security question: if we run A100 MIG slices on shared hardware, what is your isolation assurance and can we get dedicated host attestations?

Also, can you include an explicit plan for the canary (expected RPS, duration, rollback criteria)? We want that in the MAP appendix as well.

Subject: Re: MAP kickoff — perf benchmarks to lock timeline & HW recs for Acme

James — thanks for the checks. Per MAP appendix (attached) and answers below: 

1) Warm pools vs failover: recommendation is hybrid routing. For the latency-critical 10% lane we will provision a small warm pool of 3 H100 full GPUs (reserved) to meet cold-start constraints. For bulk traffic, route to A100 MIG slices with an autoscaler that can burst to H100 if p95 approaches 360ms. This gives both cost control and guard-rails for spikes.

2) Cost target: we've sketched two commercial options in the MAP appendix: 
- Option A (performance first): Reserved H100 + mixed A100 capacity — estimated effective cost per 1M tokens = $Z1 (e.g., higher but within procurement exception).
- Option B (cost-first): A100 MIG heavy with occasional H100 burst — estimated cost per 1M tokens = $Z2 (meets your $Y target in the steady-state assumption). Exact pricing will be included in the SOW.

3) Security for MIG: MIG runs on dedicated tenancy instances in our Dedicated plan; we provide host attestations and SOC2 evidence. For customers requiring absolute hardware isolation, we can offer Dedicated Full-GPU tenancy. See security appendix link in MAP.

Canary plan (proposed):
- Duration: 72 hours (staged)
- Target RPS: 350 peak, steady 120 RPS
- Acceptance: p95 <= 400ms, error rate < 0.5% for 12h rolling window
- Rollback: auto-rollback if p95 > 500ms for 10 minutes or error rate > 1% sustained 5 minutes.

Next steps: final MAP v1 (attached acme_map_v1.pdf updated) + perf CSV and cost matrix attached. I'll schedule the sync for 2026-09-07 at 10am PT. If you sign off on Option A vs B, we can finalize the SOW and DocuSign link (DocuSign: DS-554333).

Attachments: perf_summary_20260901.csv, latency_vs_cost_matrix.xlsx, acme_map_v1.pdf
